transcript.text: In this data visualization, you can see an earthquake strike under the Pacific Ocean and purple,
and the tsunami it generated in white. The red, orange, yellow, and green ringlets you see here
are in part atmospheric disturbances caused by the event. Every ringlet you see is a real-time
reading from ground stations around the globe. The disturbances were picked up by NASA's
experimental system Guardian just eight minutes after the earthquake. In Hawaii, Guardian flashes red
and orange as it picks up the incoming wave, 32 minutes before the tsunami makes landfall and is
detected by the tidal gauges seen here in blue. There's no stopping the tsunami, but NASA's Guardian
could provide communities precious time to prepare.
